about: Tests that fail when run against the phone's API code (public/local-api.js) instead of server.js. Every entry is a difference by design; real differences are fixed, not listed (plan step 1.2). run-tests.js (pass 2) fails on any failure NOT listed here, and on any listed test that passes or no longer exists. Kinds: 'dev-server only' = tests a feature only the PC dev server has (no phone equivalent); 'platform' = each platform answers for itself on purpose.

differences.test: desktop /api/storage: database size, no app storage limit
differences.why: The test expects the desktop answer (mode 'desktop'); the phone answers mode 'phone' with its own storage limit. Each platform reports its own storage.

differences.test: Cache-Control: app JS/CSS revalidate and are NEVER immutable
differences.why: Static-file caching headers come from the dev server; on the phone the pages are served by the Android WebView from the app package.

differences.test: Cache-Control: HTML file and clean-URL route are no-cache
differences.why: As above: page caching headers are a dev-server feature.

differences.test: Cache-Control: only vendor/** and fonts/*.woff2 are immutable
differences.why: As above: page caching headers are a dev-server feature.
Checks page routes on the dev server; the phone code only answers /api requests.

differences.test: server.js marks its pages and API answers as the dev server
differences.why: Checks the dev server's own page and header marking.

differences.test: default mode: loopback Host names are accepted
differences.why: The LAN gate (Host check, token, hardening headers) protects the PC dev server's network port; the phone has no network port. The whole file needs a real listening server.

differences.test: default mode: any other Host is refused with 403 (DNS rebinding)
LAN mode: a bare IPv4 Host is accepted, a domain name still is not
hardening headers are on every response
LAN mode: another machine without the token gets 401
LAN mode: a wrong token (Bearer, cookie or query) gets 401
LAN mode: the right token by Bearer header or cookie lets the request through
LAN mode: ?token= sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie and redirects the token out of the URL
LAN mode: requests from this PC itself never need the token
accessConfig: loopback hosts are not LAN mode; anything else is
differences.why: A server.js unit test, but in a file whose setup starts a listening server, so it cannot run on the phone target.

differences.test: startup: LAN mode without a long enough PLANNR_TOKEN refuses to start
differences.why: Tests server.js start-up: dev server only.
